# Purnendu Dash

> Founder and product architect behind MultiVendorX, DualCube and VuloLabs, building eCommerce and eLearning software on WordPress and WooCommerce. Based in Kolkata, West Bengal, India.

I'm a product founder and system builder. I work at the intersection of ecommerce, marketplace platforms, and learning management systems, designing practical, scalable solutions for real operational problems.

## Key facts

- Name: Purnendu Dash
- Role: Founder & CEO
- Location: Kolkata, West Bengal, India
- Key offering: Technology Advisory (senior technical leadership for marketplace, learning, and WordPress or WooCommerce businesses)
- eCommerce: MultiVendorX, CatalogX, Notifima
- eLearning: DualCube, MooWoodle
- VuloLabs ecosystem: VuloMail, VuloPilot, VuloForm
- Companies: MultiVendorX (since 2015), DualCube (since 2011), TechMonastic (founded 2014)
- WordPress.org contributor since 2009; contributed to WordPress core releases 4.9 and 5.1
- WordCamp speaker and organizer

## Articles

- [Why most WooCommerce marketplaces get vendor payouts wrong](https://purnendudash.com/blog/vendor-payouts-woocommerce-marketplaces): Why commission and payouts break first as a WooCommerce store becomes a marketplace, and how a rule-based design avoids a rebuild.
- [LMS and ecommerce do not have to be separate systems](https://purnendudash.com/blog/lms-and-ecommerce-dont-have-to-be-separate): Why selling courses means keeping a store and an LMS in sync, and how designing them as one system avoids broken enrollments and refunds.
- [Fifteen years of building an open source WordPress plugin](https://purnendudash.com/blog/fifteen-years-open-source-wordpress-plugin): What fifteen years of maintaining MultiVendorX taught about backward compatibility, community support and contributing to WordPress core.
- [A founder's guide to multi-vendor commission models](https://purnendudash.com/blog/founders-guide-multi-vendor-commission-models): Flat, tiered or category-based: how each marketplace commission model affects which vendors join and stay, and how to keep it adjustable.
- [Speaking at WordCamp: lessons from organizing and presenting](https://purnendudash.com/blog/speaking-at-wordcamp-lessons): What organizing and speaking at WordCamp taught about talking to store owners and developers: lead with the problem, not the plugin.
